The boy wakes up slowly, opening his eyes to the light streaming fiercely through the window he had left open the night before to let in some air. He didn’t consider that if he didn’t fully lower the blind, the light would wake him early in the morning. He sits up in bed for a few seconds, in his underwear, staring at the slats of the blind as the light mercilessly pierces through, as if trying to understand where he is and who he is. Gradually, he becomes aware of his body and starts to feel his dry tongue after several hours of uninterrupted sleep. He decides to get up to have some juice, and this time an immense wave of light floods every corner, revealing the house’s imperfections—the dust accumulating in the corners of the furniture, the TV remote abandoned haphazardly on the couch.

His eyes fully open when he’s greeted by his dog, who had been dozing on a cushion in a corner near his room, wondering where the person who scratches behind his ears and fills his bowl with treats has gone and why he’s taking so long to come out. Finally, his dog’s unease ends as he leaps onto the boy, happily wagging his tail. They head to the kitchen together, hoping for a reward.

The boy scratches his head, distracted, thinking about the day ahead. First, he’ll have some breakfast and play that video game that has him quite hooked. Then, he’ll head to the beach with a towel and flip-flops to see who’s free for a swim. With no more concern in his mind than seeing how the beach water is today, he’s earned his vacation; August is a sticky and grateful month, tasting like lemon ice cream and wet skin. The school year has felt extremely long, with that peculiar perception of time in youth, where hours stretch out and one has time to get bored.

He walks down the street to the beach, barely ten minutes from his house, hoping to run into that girl who stirs his thoughts and keeps him awake many nights, mentally replaying their last encounters: What did she mean by that look, that gesture? It seems like she brushed against me on purpose, but then why does she look at the other guy? Surely she knows I like her, but still, she doesn’t do anything, or at least that’s how it seems to me. All my friends say she’s into me, but I can’t find the right moment... I’m afraid of making a mistake and messing it up, but it’s so hot, and it’s so nice in the water that I’d like to hold her tight so she doesn’t slip away.

With these thoughts in mind, he meets one of his friends already bouncing a beach ball on the ground, waiting for the chance to throw it hard. It’s remarkable how teenagers have an irresistible urge to kick things. Without too many formal greetings, they start running, already on the sand, and dive into the water, leaving behind the few things they carry—towel, flip-flops, ball...

As he plunges into the cold water, his mind clears quickly, and all traces of the morning’s sluggishness vanish. He opens his eyes wide and looks at the sky, his wet hair sticking to his face. He stretches his muscles, opens his arms wide as if trying to embrace the entire sea with his stroke, and for a moment, he thinks of nothing else. He closes his eyes, submerges, takes a couple of strong strokes towards the bottom, and opens his eyes to see water that, though not crystal clear, is quite clean in the early morning. He surfaces again to receive a big hug from his friend, who tries to dunk his head underwater. They struggle, play, scratch, and hurt each other, but they laugh, laugh out loud. They get out onto the sand and start kicking the ball hard as the rest of the gang, including the girls, begin to join in. A key thought flashes through his mind: Is she here today? He missteps while kicking, trips, and falls clumsily. The rest of the gang sees his clumsiness from a distance and runs over excitedly to pile on top of him. They greet each other warmly, get annoyed with one another, and reproach each other for little things.

The girls, a bit more orderly, lay out their towels, sarongs, and bags neatly. Some pull out teen gossip magazines and lie on their towels, overcoming the initial shyness of taking off their shirts. In a few seconds, they’re absorbed in their favorite celebrities’ trivialities, announced loudly in the glossy pages of their magazines. Meanwhile, the boys focus on an impromptu soccer game on the sand, with no other goal than to impress their girls and stand out from the rest of the pack in the few awkward ways they know. The girls recognize their clumsiness but enjoy feeling admired and have fun. They pretend not to care and keep their eyes on their magazines, conversations, or music, but they keep a close watch on their chosen boy’s progress out of the corner of their eyes, harboring a deep, novel-like nineteenth-century love for him.

Soon, the boys are exhausted. Running under the scorching midday sun is a tough toll that spares no one, though our boy had long been wandering the sand, more focused on finding his girl’s gaze than on the ball. She knows it, and soon decides he’s suffered enough and suggests to the girls that they go into the water.

They enter the water carefully; there’s a bit of wind, and the water is very cold. The boys quickly catch the hint, abandon the ball, and rush into the water noisily, splashing everyone in their path, pushing the girls and being a nuisance. Again, they’re clumsy in their attempts to get close to the opposite sex. Small groups form in the water, and everyone seems clear about who they prefer to be with. They play at dunking each other; the bolder ones lift a girl onto their shoulders, creating an excessive intimacy both will remember for hours.

Afterward, the boy sits next to his girl, mustering all his courage, and shows interest in what she’s looking at in her magazine. He makes an immense effort to understand what she’s talking about, wishing he were more up-to-date on these things, telling himself he plays that video game too much, and that he should listen more to his sister when she talks about these boring things at dinner.

He barely passes the test, and the girl tells herself that maybe he’s not such a disaster and rewards him with a few casual touches on the arm and shoulder that will keep the boy awake for several hours that night.

Running home, he takes a shower and has a light lunch because it’s very hot, and they have plans to go to the movies in the afternoon. What movie? It doesn’t matter, whatever is showing; the important thing is to be skillful enough to sit close to his girl, though our boy doesn’t suspect that the seats have long been assigned, and certainly, neither he nor the rest of his crude buddies have had anything to do with it. The girls spend many hours talking about them and dividing up the pie more or less fairly because they also have their hierarchies, their methods, and their cruelties.

Our boy finds himself sitting next to his girl in the darkness of the cinema, not quite sure why. He tries not to spill popcorn on her and stays alert. He watches the screen but is much more attentive to what’s happening around him. He tries to whisper witty and funny comments about the scenes to make her laugh quietly. He makes the most of the scarce two hours of semi-darkness and semi-intimacy that the theater provides. Time flies, and he must bring out his best to impress her. You never know what little detail might tip the balance in his favor or someone else’s. Or at least, that’s what he thinks. He stakes his life on every breath, he can’t fail. He wants to be daring and spends what seems like an eternity deciding whether to do it or not, but finally, he goes for it and touches her hand when she reaches for the soda they share. She looks at him, and he takes a deep breath of courage, making it clear that the contact wasn’t accidental, shattering his heart (which stops for a few seconds) and takes her hand. Trembling but determined, with desire and fear at the same time. She looks at the screen, as if downplaying the matter, wanting to project an image of confidence far from the reality. But she’s very convincing, and he thinks, "at least she didn’t pull her hand away." But she seems to know exactly what she’s doing, and despite her heart racing at a thousand beats per second, she manages to keep her cool and lets a few seemingly eternal seconds pass before responding to the gesture and moving her hand to fit with his, accepting the gesture and triggering a multitude of sensations that run through their bodies from head to toe, as if a lightning bolt had struck from the theater ceiling directed straight at them.

He looks at the screen too, very serious, as if something very significant had just happened, and for a few minutes, they are two teenagers, holding hands, staring at a movie screen showing things they can’t comprehend because their minds are racing wildly, at cruising speed. The physical sensations overwhelm them, mixed with insane dreams of unimaginable futures that only young minds can contain. On the screen, Delilah shaves Samson’s hair, but no one seems to care much.

Night falls quickly, and the fine beach sand awaits them again, this time with sweaters over their shoulders to keep warm and an improvised bonfire in a sand hollow. They sit in circles around the light, seeking intimacy, forced at first, feeling like shipwrecked sailors adrift in the open sea, clinging to a small floating piece of wood. The firelight casts eerie shadows on their faces, revealing the fierce tan from the sun taken that morning—of that newly minted skin, with only a few years of life.

The boy feels very hot, a fire under his skin because, of course, he forgot to apply sunscreen again that morning, as his mother insists daily. But he hides it because she’s close, and he must appear his best self once more. He sits in the cold sand, burying his feet to feel its refreshing effect even more. He looks at the sea, black as a wolf’s mouth, and closes his eyes for a moment, letting his imagination run wild. It takes him on unknown paths of uncertain futures, filled with illusions where one can be whatever one wants. He imagines himself doing wonderful things, embarking on fascinating projects. He feels the sea breeze on his face, the salty water smell, the crackling firewood, the sand’s touch on his toes, and thinks the only thing that could improve this moment is a kiss—the kiss he’s dreamed of all summer, this hot and humid August that has seeped into his bones for life. He feels a bit shy and doesn’t dare seek his precious treasure, so he limits himself to fantasizing again, imagining those small, salty, candy-flavored lips touching his clumsily but with a tender, newly awakened passion.

Lost in his thoughts, he suddenly feels knees digging into the sand behind him and hands covering his eyes. Quickly, he perceives that sweet perfume he knows so well, as a familiar, longed-for voice whispers in his ear: "Guess who?"
